reason: The README clearly defines the plugin as a DeepSeek Harness workload manager for workspace-owned long-running processes, with a Runtime Center UI and host APIs for lifecycle management plus optional agent tools. This makes its primary user-facing purpose process automation and operational control rather than code generation, search, or content/document workflows.

summaries.zh: DSH Workloads 为 DeepSeek Harness 提供会话外的工作区级长期运行进程管理能力，在运行中心界面和 workload 工具中支持查看、启动、等待就绪、读取日志、重启与停止。
summaries.en: DSH Workloads adds workspace-owned long-running process management to DeepSeek Harness, letting users monitor and control workloads through a Runtime Center UI and workload tools.

capabilities: Manages long-running local processes through start/stop/restart/list/log/wait operations.
Enables process control via Agent tools (`workload_*`) in configured presets.
Displays workload status, health, PID, and log tails in a Runtime Center UI.
Persists workload metadata and run identity outside project repositories with session-authorized API access.
Includes local-process restrictions and workspace-bound command execution checks.

reasons.code: The plugin exposes a host service with lifecycle methods such as start, wait, logs, stop, restart, and list for workspace workloads.
It registers a Runtime Center conversation view and presents workload readiness, phase, health, PID, and log tail information with stop/restart controls.
The tools package exposes agent-facing workload management tools (`workload_list`, `workload_start`, `workload_wait`, `workload_logs`, `workload_stop`, `workload_stop_all`, `workload_restart`).
Local-process safety notes include command filtering, workspace-bound cwd checks, environment scrubbing, and controlled Windows process termination behavior.
